details: A request is resolved to one canonical workspace before routing, and every persisted read/write scope is repository-relative to that root.
Relative scopes retain the canonical run root, including normal non-Git fixture directories.
Absolute scopes outside the run root require an identical canonical Git common directory and exact membership in the run repository's registered worktree list.
Unrelated repositories, non-Git outside paths, base-plus-linked scopes, two-linked-worktree scopes, and symlink escapes fail closed with a safe generic mismatch detail.
An adversarial directory with a copied linked-worktree .git pointer is rejected during initial resolution and persisted-root reverification.
Absolute protected scopes are converted to root-relative form before the pure router checks them; an independent linked-worktree .env probe routed driver/protected-scope.
The resolver does not alter authority, capability, risk, budget, or provider policy decisions beyond supplying the verified root-relative request.
The route decision durably stores canonical workspace root plus relative read/write scopes.
The governess reloads the routed journal record and re-verifies registration/common-directory identity before detached spawn.
The detached worker derives the original run root from the manifest, re-verifies the persisted workspace, and constructs its broker and prompt request from the verified root and scopes.
Guarded patch application independently repeats persisted-root verification and applies within the adopted worktree boundary.
Regression tests prove linked-worktree reads return linked content rather than base content and guarded apply changes only the linked checkout.
Active write claims are workspace-qualified and use persisted normalized write scopes.
Two edits to the same linked-worktree file produce one utility route and one driver/write-conflict route.
The same relative filename in the base checkout and a linked worktree does not create a false conflict, and the claim-time store gate uses the same workspace-aware boundary.
Independent focused task-router, utility-runtime, utility-store, utility-tools, and utility-workspace suite passed 87/87.

known_limitations: The worktree registration parser intentionally ignores stale registrations whose paths cannot be canonicalized, so they cannot become execution roots.
The live loop-47 delivery confirmation is recorded separately from this source-level adoption evaluation.
notes: PASS. Independent review initially found workspace-unaware write claims and a copied-.git registration spoof. Both were corrected and regression-covered before this final verdict.
